title: Book 5 — Terpsichore, Chapter 122
paragraphs: These Persians, then, were destroyed in this way; and meanwhile Hymaees, who was another of those pursuing the Ionians who had marched on Sardis, directed his march to the Propontis and took Cius in Mysia. Having taken this city, when he was informed that Daurises had left the Hellespont and was marching against Caria, he left the Propontis and led his army to the Hellespont; and he conquered all the Aeolians who occupy the district of Ilium, and also the Gergithae, who were left as a remnant of the ancient Teucrians. While conquering these tribes, Hymaees himself ended his life from sickness in the land of Troas.
